n-m-e1-s2b-03.title: Count Beads on String by Color
n-m-e1-s2b-03.goal: When repeating color rule for one string end halfway through one set, learn say you must also count leftover beads by color, and see how each color number change as bead number change.

n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose only di first line for Minho solution wey wrong.
n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s1.hint.0: Draw di 8 beads and count red ones and blue ones separately.
n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether adding di red and blue numbers Minho talk about give 8 beads altogether.

n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s1.line.1: If you see “red, blue, blue” as one set, di 8 beads get two sets and 2 extra beads.
n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s1.line.2: One set get 1 red and 2 blue, so two sets get 2 red and 4 blue.

n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s2.prompt: If you string 10 beads with same rule, how many blue beads go dey?

n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s2.r.c: Dis thinking guess say na half of beads. Check whether blue and red beads equal in number.

n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s2.explain: If di set red, blue, blue come three times, na 9 beads, and di 10th bead red. Red na 3+1=4 and blue na 6.
n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s3.prompt: String beads with same rule starting from red. Find three different bead counts n where blue beads exactly 2 times red beads. (At least 7 and at most 20 beads.)
n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s3.hint.0: Change bead number to 7, 8, 9, ... and write in table how many red and blue beads dey each time.
n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s3.hint.1: Gather bead counts where blue na 2 times red, and see wetin dem get in common.
n-m-e1-s2b-03.s.s3.ok.c1: At least 7 and at most 20 beads.

n-m-e1-s2b-04.title: How Many Cookies Fit Remain?
n-m-e1-s2b-04.goal: For subtraction story, follow how possible range for remaining number dey get smaller each time new information come, and find di boundary where both amounts become equal.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.material: Cookies dey on plate. When person eat some, number of cookies left change. You wan find how many cookies remain after Minji eat. Dem go give more information one piece at a time.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.thinking.0: Show Wetin You Never Know as a Range
n-m-e1-s2b-04.thinking.1: Narrow di Possible Numbers with New Information
n-m-e1-s2b-04.thinking.2: Find di Boundary Where Dem Become Equal
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.prompt: Each time dem tell you something new, choose wetin you fit say about di cookies wey remain.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.hint.0: Show how many cookies dey at beginning and how many story say dem eat, with picture or words.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.hint.1: Add di new information to di story and compare whether your earlier idea still correct.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.0.info: 6 cookies dey on plate. Minji eat some cookies. You no know yet how many e eat.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.0.ask: How many cookies remain for plate?
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.0.after: If you no know how many dem eat, you no fit decide one exact number left. Still, you know say e less than 6.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Minji eat some, so cookies don reduce. E no fit still be 6.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.0.o.b: I no know how many, but less than 6 remain.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Once dem eat cookies, na fewer remain. More no fit remain pass how many dey at start.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Dis thinking decide say na only 1 dem eat. You no know how many dem eat yet.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.1.info: E turn out say cookies wey remain pass cookies wey dem eat. You still no know how many dem eat.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.1.after: If dem eat 1 cookie, 5 remain; if dem eat 2, 4 remain, so more remain than dem eat. If dem eat 3, 3 remain, so both equal. So 4 or 5 cookies remain.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: If 3 cookies remain, dem don eat 3 too, so more no remain than dem eat.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: If 1 cookie remain, dem don eat 5. Check whether more remain than dem eat.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Dis thinking no use di new information dem give.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.2.ask: How many cookies remain? Also check whether e fit wetin you find earlier.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.2.after: If you eat 2 from 6, 4 remain. 4 dey inside “4 or 5” wey you find earlier, so both statements agree.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Check whether you mix am with case wey dem eat 3.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.st.2.r.d: Dis thinking add 2 to 6. When dem eat cookies, fewer remain.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s1.reflect: At first, you only know say fewer than 6 cookies remain. Each new information narrow di possible number to 4 or 5, and after you know how many cookies dem eat, one number remain. Explain how your thinking narrow each time more information come.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s2.prompt: Dis time 10 cookies dey for plate. Minji eat at least 1, and more cookies remain than dem eat. Choose numbers a for cookies eaten and b for cookies remaining in three different ways.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s2.hint.0: Choose number of cookies eaten, then work out how many remain if dem eat that number from 10.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s2.hint.1: Put number remaining and number eaten side by side and compare which one bigger.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s2.fail.c1: Make cookies eaten a whole number at least 1, and cookies remaining a number at least 0.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s2.ok.c2: Cookies eaten and cookies remaining add up to 10.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s2.fail.c2: Cookies eaten and cookies remaining must add up to di 10 cookies at start.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s2.ok.c3: More cookies remain than dem eat.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s2.fail.c3: More cookies no remain than dem eat.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s2.explain: If dem eat 1, 2, 3, or 4 cookies, 9, 8, 7, or 6 remain, so more remain. If dem eat 5, 5 remain too, so more no remain.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s3.prompt: Out of 10 cookies, how many cookies dem must eat so more remain than dem eat? (Dem eat at least 1 cookie.)
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s3.hint.0: Increase number of cookies eaten one by one from 1, and write in table how number remaining change.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s3.hint.1: Find when remaining cookies and eaten cookies become same.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s3.r.a: If dem eat 5 cookies, 5 remain too, so both same.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s3.r.b: If dem eat more cookies, fewer remain. Check how many remain if dem eat 6.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s3.o.c: E only need to be less than 10.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s3.r.c: If dem eat 9, only 1 cookie remain.
n-m-e1-s2b-04.s.s3.explain: If dem eat 1, 2, 3, or 4 cookies, more remain; if 5, same number; if 6 or more, fewer remain. So dem must eat fewer than 5. Di boundary na 5, wey split 10 into two equal parts.

n-m-e1-s2-01.title: Find di Numbers Wey Fit Enter di Number Box

n-m-e1-s2-01.goal: Choose numbers wey meet condition "greater than ... and less than ...", make some examples yourself, and count how many numbers meet am altogether in number order.
n-m-e1-s2-01.material: We dey play number box game. Sign for box say "Put only numbers wey pass 70 and less than 80." You go try put number cards inside one by one.
n-m-e1-s2-01.thinking.0: Check meaning of condition (greater, less) one by one
n-m-e1-s2-01.thinking.1: Make examples wey meet condition and check dem
n-m-e1-s2-01.thinking.2: Count without missing any or adding extra

n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose all number cards wey fit go inside box.

n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s1.r.c: 79 pass 70 and e less than 80. Write numbers in order and check.

n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s2.hint.1: Among dem, circle numbers wey ones digit pass 5.
n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s2.ok.c1: E pass 70 and e less than 80.
n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s2.fail.c1: E no pass 70 and less than 80. Write numbers in order and ask one by one whether dem meet condition.
n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s2.explain: 76, 77, 78, and 79 all correct. 70 and 80 get 0 for ones place, so dem no pass 5, and dem no meet "pass 70" or "less than 80" too.
n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s3.prompt: Dis time no condition for ones place. How many numbers altogether dey pass 70 and less than 80?
n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s3.hint.0: Leave out 70 and 80, and write numbers between dem one by one in order.
n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s3.hint.1: Point each number wey you write and count dem.

n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s3.r.b: Dis count every number from 70 to 80, including both ends.
n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s3.r.c: Dis count by writing in order di numbers wey meet condition.
n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s3.r.d: Dis subtract di two end numbers, then subtract one again.
n-m-e1-s2-01.s.s3.explain: 9 numbers dey: 71, 72, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, 79. Di 10 wey you get from 80 minus 70 na distance between two ends, wey different from number of numbers between dem.

n-m-e1-s2b-02.title: After How Many Cards Go the Picture Cards Look the Same?
n-m-e1-s2b-02.goal: For rule wey two things dey change together, like shape and color, check by arranging cards say one thing wey dey repeat no mean the whole card dey repeat.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.material: Jiho dey arrange picture cards in one row. The shapes dey take turns between ○ and □, and the colors dey go red, blue, yellow in order. The 1st na red ○, the 2nd na blue □, and the 3rd na yellow ○. Jiho talk, 'The colors repeat every three cards, so the same card go come every three cards.'
n-m-e1-s2b-02.thinking.0: Check a claim wey look at only one feature but talk about everything
n-m-e1-s2b-02.thinking.1: Find counterexample by arranging the cards yourself
n-m-e1-s2b-02.thinking.2: Compare how long each of the two rules take to come round

n-m-e1-s2b-02.prereq.1: Know Words for Order (which one: first, second, ...)
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you think about wetin Jiho talk? Draw di 4th card by following di rules, then decide.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s1.hint.0: Write only di colors of cards 1 to 4 first, then separately write only di shapes.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s1.hint.1: Put di 4th card beside di 1st card and compare color and shape one by one.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s1.o.a: Correct. Di 4th card go be red ○ too.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s1.r.a: Think back whether you decide di 4th card color and shape separately. Di shape change every two cards.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s1.o.b: Wrong. Di 4th card red, but e shape na □.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s1.o.c: Wrong. Di rule for how di colors go round wrong from di beginning.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s1.r.c: Di question don give you di color rule. Check di reason wey you say e wrong by using di 4th card.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s1.o.d: I no fit tell. I need lay out more cards.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s1.r.d: Di rules don set, so you fit tell wetin di 4th card be. Continue di colors and shapes one after di other.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s1.explain: Di 4th card color return to red, but shapes alternate ○, □, ○, □, so e na □. So di 4th card no be same as di 1st. One thing matching no mean di whole card match.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s2.prompt: For which number di first card wey get same color and same shape as di 1st card appear?
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s2.hint.0: Draw cards up to di 7th. Under each number, write di color and shape together.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s2.hint.1: Circle di cards wey get same color and same shape as di 1st card.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s2.r.a: Di 3rd card yellow. Check whether di color different.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s2.r.b: Di 4th card get different shape. Think back wetin you check earlier.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s2.r.c: Compare di color and shape of di 6th card with di 1st.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s2.explain: If you arrange di cards in order: red ○, blue □, yellow ○, red □, blue ○, yellow □, red ○. Di 7th na di first card wey look exactly like di 1st. Colors return every 3 cards and shapes every 2, so e take 6 cards before both return together.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s3.prompt: Dis time shapes alternate between ○ and □, and colors alternate between red and blue. Di 1st red ○ and di 2nd blue □. After how many cards di same card go repeat?
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s3.hint.0: Draw di 3rd and 4th cards and compare dem with di 1st and 2nd.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s3.hint.1: Write separately how many cards it take for shapes to return and for colors to return, then compare dem.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s3.r.b: Dis thinking use di 3 cards from previous question as they be. Draw di 3rd card of dis row yourself.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s3.r.c: Dis thinking add 2 cards for shapes and 2 for colors. Check how di 3rd card compare with di 1st.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s3.r.d: Dis thinking use di 6 cards from previous question as they be. For dis row, di rule length different.
n-m-e1-s2b-02.s.s3.explain: Both shapes and colors return every 2 cards, so di 3rd card red ○, exactly same as di 1st. If both rules return after same length, cards repeat after that length. If lengths different (2 and 3 earlier), e take longer.

n-m-e1-s1-01.title: Which of the two cups get more water?
n-m-e1-s1-01.goal: Find the mistake wey happen when you compare water for containers of different shapes just by how high the water look. Then find a fair way to compare, and make examples wey height go give wrong answer.
n-m-e1-s1-01.material: Minjae get two cups in front. Cup 가 narrow and tall. Cup 나 wide and short. Water dey inside both cups, and the water for cup 가 reach higher. Minjae wan find which cup get more water.
n-m-e1-s1-01.thinking.0: Separating wetin you see from wetin you guess
n-m-e1-s1-01.thinking.1: Pouring the water to measure am with the same standard and compare
n-m-e1-s1-01.prereq.0: Knowing the shapes of containers wey fit hold water
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s1.prompt: Minjae talk. Choose the first line wey no correct.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s1.hint.0: For each line, sort am as "something I see with my eyes" or "something I guess from wetin I see."
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s1.hint.1: Think whether a statement wey depend on height go still correct when the two cups get the same shape and when dem get different shapes.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s1.line.0: Cup 가 narrow and tall, and cup 나 wide and short.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s1.line.1: The water for cup 가 reach higher than the water for cup 나.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s1.line.2: So cup 가 get more water inside.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s1.line.3: Even if the cups get different shapes, the one wey water reach higher get more.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s1.explain: Lines 1 and 2 talk wetin person see, just as e be. The first mistake dey line 3. Narrow cup fit fill high with small water. If cups get different shapes, you no fit know the water amount by looking at height alone. Line 4 extend the idea for line 3 to all cups.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.prompt: Choose all the fair ways to compare water for the two cups.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.hint.0: Check whether dem measure the water amounts wey dem dey compare with the same "ruler."
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.hint.1: For each way, think whether the cup shape affect the result or e no affect am.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.o.a: Pour the water from each cup enter two empty bottles wey get the same shape, then compare the heights
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.r.a: Put the two cups side by side and look dem well for longer time
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.o.b: Use small dish to scoop water from each cup and count how many scoops
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.r.b: Decide say the cup wey outside shape bigger get more water
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.o.c: If you pour the water into containers wey get the same shape, you fit compare by height. This way good because the shapes na the same.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.r.c: Looking for longer no remove the illusion wey the shapes cause. You need way to measure with the same standard.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.o.d: This one count how many times dem fill the same small container. You fit compare no matter the cups' shapes.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.r.d: Big cup fit hold only small water. You need compare the water inside directly.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s2.explain: You no fit compare water for cups wey get different shapes by looking at the height alone. If you pour am into empty bottles wey get the same shape and compare the heights, or count how many scoops from the same small dish, you fit compare fairly.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s3.prompt: When you scoop with small dish, water for cup 가 take a scoops and water for cup 나 take b scoops. Make three different cases wey water for cup 가 reach higher but cup 나 get more water, by changing a and b. a and b na numbers from 1 to 9.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s3.hint.0: The side wey get bigger number of scoops get more water. First decide which cup suppose get bigger number of scoops.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s3.hint.1: Choose a, then choose b as number bigger than a. Then change a to another number and do am again.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s3.var.a: Water for cup 가 (how many scoops) a
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s3.var.b: Water for cup 나 (how many scoops) b
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s3.fail.c1: Abeg make a number from 1 to 9.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s3.fail.c2: Abeg make b number from 1 to 9.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s3.ok.c3: Cup 나 get more water (e get bigger number of scoops).
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s3.fail.c3: For cup 나 to get more water, the number of scoops for am must pass the number for cup 가.
n-m-e1-s1-01.s.s3.explain: The more scoops e take, the more water dey. For example, if cup 가 take 2 scoops and cup 나 take 5 scoops, cup 나 get more water even though water for cup 가 reach higher. So many examples dey where height alone give wrong answer.

n-m-e1-s2b-01.title: Na the Same Rule If the Shapes Change?
n-m-e1-s2b-01.goal: Learn say even if the shapes change, na the same rule if the same shapes dey the same places, then make several rows with that rule.
n-m-e1-s2b-01.material: Seoa arrange shape cards in one row: '○ □ □ ○ □ □ ○ □ □'. The cards na ○, □, and △. We wan find rows wey get 'the same rule' as Seoa row.

n-m-e1-s2b-01.s.s1.explain: Seoa row repeat 'one shape, then two of another shape together'. △ □ □ △ □ □ and □ ○ ○ □ ○ ○ get the same pattern too. Even if the shape types different, na the same rule if the same shapes dey the same places.
n-m-e1-s2b-01.s.s2.prompt: Make ○ mean 1, □ mean 2, and △ mean 3. Make rows wey get the same rule as Seoa row. Write first card as a, second as b, third as c, and fourth as d. Make three different rows.

n-m-e1-s2b-01.s.s2.fail.c1: You fit use only 1, 2, or 3 for the cards.

n-m-e1-s2b-01.s.s3.prompt: '○ □ □ ○ □ □' and '△ ○ ○ △ ○ ○' use different shapes. Even so, why we fit say dem get the same rule?

n-m-e1-s2b-01.s.s3.r.b: Even if the number of shapes na the same, the rules fit different. ○ □ ○ □ ○ □ get 6 too.
n-m-e1-s2b-01.s.s3.o.c: One shape come first, then two of the same shape, and this pattern dey repeat.
n-m-e1-s2b-01.s.s3.r.d: Just because the same shape dey inside no mean the rules na the same. Look at the places wey the same shapes dey.
n-m-e1-s2b-01.s.s3.explain: For both rows, 'one shape, then two of another shape' dey repeat. The rule depend on the places wey the same shapes dey, no be which shapes dem use.
